purpose: The arms, workload cells and repetition protocol of the legacy observability baseline. Every number in observability-1777-baseline.json was produced by `scripts/observability_bench.py run` against THIS file, and the run manifest carries its digest; `verify` refuses a run whose file differs. The two arms differ ONLY in celery_env (and, for the reference arm, in the settings module it boots the web tier with), which is what makes their difference the overhead answer rather than a difference in work.

protocol.notes: repeats=7 and seed=20261121 are the conventions of scripts/task_perf_runner.sh (#1396): seven repetitions of a seeded workload is what its cv, its stability floor and its gate read, so the web-tier cells use the same figure instead of inventing a second one. warmup_requests is excluded from the measured samples but recorded as its own phase, because the first requests of a Django process pay for imports and query-plan warm-up that no later request pays. The peer endpoint is unrouted on purpose (#1032): it walks the whole middleware chain, answers 404 on an idle server, and therefore shows what a request which does no work of its own pays for its neighbours. concurrency 8 rather than the 16 of the #1617 reading, because this measurement is about the per-request cost of a detector, not about saturating gunicorn.

arms.name: diagnostics-off
arms.definition: Nothing of the technical observability is enabled: no task profiler (#1389), no performance recorder (#1391), no exporter (#1392), no capacity telemetry (#1401). For the web-tier cells the arm additionally boots the backend with legacy_off_settings_module, which drops system.logging.middleware.LogSlowRequestsMiddleware out of the chain - there is no knob which turns that middleware's per-request SQL capture off, so an honest 'diagnostics off' reading of the HTTP tier has to remove it rather than claim it is idle.

arms.name: legacy-shipped
arms.definition: The detector/profiler stack as it shipped, with its own documented defaults: the sampling profiler of #1389 on the four measured task families, the performance recorder of #1391, the capacity telemetry of #1401. The values are the settings.py defaults (sample rate 0.05, memory ceiling 128 MiB, memory sample 0.5 s) because a baseline which silently tuned the knobs would be measuring a configuration nobody runs. The HTTP tier boots with the shipped middleware chain, so LogSlowRequestsMiddleware and its slow-request dumps are part of this arm.

cells.name: harvesting-import
cells.notes: The bounded import chunk of #859/#895 over the backlog - the representative large-CSW-harvest work of the issue, since a harvest is this task repeated per page. Declared contract: 4 statements per unit, so its query-count column has something to be compared against.
cells.workload: synthetic md-metadata-file rows seeded by the bench class, seeded by --seed

cells.name: harvesting-fan-out
cells.notes: The catalogue round trip and the fan-out over the download queue - the half of a CSW harvest which talks to the remote and dispatches, where a duplicate remote call would first show up. Contract: 0 statements and 0 http calls per unit, so anything above the floor is the instrumentation's own work.

cells.name: monitoring-probe
cells.notes: The concurrent-task cell: probe checks are a fan-out over the monitoring queue, so queue wait matters as much as active time, and this is the family whose work is HTTP-bound (1 http call, 7 statements per unit). The issue's 'concurrent tasks' is read as a fan-out of a fan-out, measured rather than asserted.
cells.workload: synthetic GetMap probes against a mocked OGC client (patched-ogc-client-200)

cells.name: housekeeping
cells.notes: The retention sweeps - attempt retention, slow-request dump retention, capacity snapshot rebuild. It is in the protocol because one of the things it retains IS the storage the baseline measures: an arm which writes more dumps also makes this task do more work, and a baseline which omitted it would hide part of the cost of the shipped detectors.
cells.workload: synthetic attempt rows and dump files, seeded by --seed

cells.name: service-list
cells.notes: The service-list half of the issue's 'service lists/search': weighted unauthenticated list reads over keep-alive connections, the same endpoint mix and weighting the #1617 reading used, so the two are comparable. The media paths are the directories the shipped chain writes into: slow-request dumps and security-proxy analysis logs, counted before and after the phase.

cells.name: proxy
cells.notes: The proxy half of the issue. The UUID is deliberately absent: what is measured is the middleware and proxy-decision cost of a request which the layer then refuses, not MapServer's rendering, and an absent service is a deterministic 4xx which no arm can win or lose by seeding data. The weighted 4:1 against a list read keeps the proxy path dominant while still exercising the chain the list cell measures.

cells.name: service-list-ws
cells.notes: The concurrent-task shape of the web tier: 25 authenticated websockets held open for at least 75 s across the list load, which is #1617's 'no stuck websockets' acceptance expressed as a measured closed_early count rather than an assertion. knox caps live tokens per user at five (#1450), so this cell must reuse one token across arms - the tool fetches it once per run, which is why the credentials name one user.
